predictions.selection_reason: Python arguments -> parsed as strings without validation -> may lead to invalid point coordinates or scalar causing undefined behavior
predictions.source_summary: Python function arguments parsed as raw strings (x, y coordinates and scalar d) without validation
predictions.sink_summary: mpz_init_set_str() in buildPoint() and buildCurve() which can fail or cause undefined behavior on invalid numeric strings
predictions.guard_summary: No validation of string inputs before passing to GMP mpz_init_set_str(); PyArg_ParseTuple only validates string type, not numeric format
predictions.risk_pattern: Untrusted Python string inputs passed directly to GMP mpz_init_set_str() without validation, allowing invalid numeric formats that can cause undefined behavior
enclosing_conditions: Only PyArg_ParseTuple basic string type check
predictions.context_summary: Function parses three string arguments for elliptic curve point multiplication: x,y coordinates and scalar d, all passed to GMP arbitrary-precision arithmetic functions without format validation
unresolved_facts: Specific behavior of mpz_init_set_str() on malformed numeric strings
Whether pointMul() has internal validation for curve point coordinates
Potential memory safety impacts of GMP failures

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: unvalidated string input passed to GMP mpz_init_set_str causing undefined behavior on invalid numeric format
